canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_exact ∈ O_exact, where O_exact is the set of exact analytic descriptions of the two-excitation trajectory |ψ(t)⟩, its Wick-rotated Laplace-transformed amplitudes, spectral singularities, decay components, and bound-state amplitudes for two adjacent initially excited quantum emitters coupled to an infinite one-dimensional single-band waveguide
canonical_goal.target_object: An exact analytic end-state description of the two-excitation decay dynamics generated by H/ℏ = Δ∑_{j=1}^{2}a_j†a_j − J∑_{j∈ℤ}(b_j†b_{j+1}+b_j b_{j+1}†) + g∑_{j=1}^{2}(a_jb_j†+a_j†b_j), where J>0, g>0, Δ∈ℝ, a_j† creates one excitation in emitter j∈{1,2}, b_j† creates one bosonic excitation at waveguide site j∈ℤ, the emitters occupy adjacent waveguide sites j=1 and j=2, the waveguide dispersion is ω_q=−2Jcos(qd) for q∈(−π/d,π/d], and the initial state is |ψ(0)⟩=a_1†a_2†|0⟩
feasibility_constraints: The physical system consists of exactly two identical quantum emitters at adjacent sites j=1 and j=2 of an infinite one-dimensional lattice waveguide with period d>0, hopping J>0, emitter-waveguide coupling g>0, and detuning Δ∈ℝ from the centre of the single photonic band.

The Hamiltonian conserves excitation number, so |ψ(t)⟩ remains in the two-excitation subspace spanned by a_1†a_2†|0⟩, b_j†b_{j'}†|0⟩ for j,j'∈ℤ with j<j', (1/√2)b_j†b_j†|0⟩ for j∈ℤ, and a_m†b_j†|0⟩ for m∈{1,2} and j∈ℤ.

The two-excitation trajectory has the expansion |ψ(t)⟩=A(t)a_1†a_2†|0⟩+∑_{j<j'}B_{j,j'}(t)b_j†b_{j'}†|0⟩+∑_{j∈ℤ}B_{j,j}(t)(1/√2)b_j†b_j†|0⟩+∑_{m∈{1,2}}∑_{j∈ℤ}C_{m,j}(t)a_m†b_j†|0⟩, with A(0)=1 and B_{j,j'}(0)=C_{m,j}(0)=0 for all allowed indices.

The phrase collective non-Markovian decay is used operationally to mean that the emitters and waveguide modes are treated as one Hamiltonian system in which emitted excitations may remain dynamically coupled to the emitters, rather than replacing the waveguide by independent memoryless exponential decay channels for the emitters alone.
The transformed amplitudes use the scaled convention 2J=1, the Wick-rotated Laplace transform f̃(ω)=−iL{f}(−iω), and the inverse transform f(t)=−(1/(2πi))∫_{−∞+i0+}^{+∞+i0+}f̃(ω)e^{−iωt}dω.

For σ∈{−1,+1}, the one-excitation transformed emitter amplitude used inside the two-excitation construction is ã_σ(ω)=[ω−Δ−σg^2+σg^2√(ω−σ)√(ω+σ)]^{−1}, with square-root branches fixed by analytic continuation from Im(ω)>0.
The analytic function C(ω,z)=∑_{j∈ℤ}C̃_{1,j}(ω)z^{1−j} encodes C̃_{1,j}(ω) as Laurent coefficients around z=0 and obeys C(ω,e^{iqd})=e^{−iqd/2}C̃_{1,q}(ω) on the unit circle.

The transformed amplitudes Ã(ω), B̃_{p,q}(ω), B̃_{q,q}(ω), and C̃_{m,q}(ω) must satisfy the transformed Schrödinger equations induced by H and |ψ(0)⟩, including Ã(ω)=1/(ω−2Δ)+(gd/(ω−2Δ))∫_{−π/d}^{π/d}(e^{−iqd/2}C̃_{2,q}(ω)+e^{iqd/2}C̃_{1,q}(ω))dq/(2π).

success_set.definition: Σ_exact={o_exact∈O_exact : o_exact supplies closed analytic transformed amplitudes Ã(ω), B̃_{p,q}(ω), B̃_{q,q}(ω), C̃_{m,q}(ω), C(ω,z), and C_σ(ω,z) that satisfy the stated transformed Schrödinger equations and whose inverse Wick-rotated Laplace transform exactly satisfies i∂_t|ψ(t)⟩=H|ψ(t)⟩/ℏ with |ψ(0)⟩=a_1†a_2†|0⟩; the singularities of Ã(ω) determine the two-excitation spectrum and decay; real poles of Ã(ω) correspond to two-excitation bound states; non-real poles on analytically continued sheets correspond to collective exponential decay components; branch points correspond to algebraic or mixed algebraic-exponential decay components; and the resulting classification contains bound states outside continua, bound states inside continua, superradiant and subradiant components, algebraic decay, mixed algebraic-exponential decay, and logarithmic corrections to algebraic decay}

robustness_scope.ambient_space: The family of infinite-dimensional two-excitation waveguide-QED problems with Hilbert subspace span{a_1†a_2†|0⟩, b_j†b_{j'}†|0⟩, (1/√2)b_j†b_j†|0⟩, a_m†b_j†|0⟩ : j,j'∈ℤ, j<j', m∈{1,2}} and Hamiltonian H/ℏ=Δ∑_{j=1}^{2}a_j†a_j−J∑_{j∈ℤ}(b_j†b_{j+1}+b_jb_{j+1}†)+g∑_{j=1}^{2}(a_jb_j†+a_j†b_j)
robustness_scope.indexing_set: {(g,Δ,J,d): g>0, Δ∈ℝ, J>0, d>0}; after imposing 2J=1 this becomes {(g,Δ,d): g>0, Δ∈ℝ, d>0}

claimed_subfamily.definition: The solved claimed subfamily consists of exactly two adjacent identical quantum emitters initially in a_1†a_2†|0⟩, locally coupled with strength g>0 to an infinite one-dimensional single-band lattice waveguide with dispersion ω_q=−2Jcos(qd), period d>0, hopping J>0, and detuning Δ∈ℝ, with dynamics restricted to the conserved two-excitation sector.

source_span.paragraph_or_line: Abstract goal sentences; Introduction final paragraph; Section II opening and Eqs. (1)-(2)
source_span.verbatim: In this paper, we present an exact solution of collective non-Markovian decay for a minimal system featuring two adjacent quantum emitters spontaneously radiating two excitations into a 1D single-band waveguide.

hinted_superfamily.definition: The hinted but unsolved superfamily consists of systems obtained by changing the initial state to a multiphoton scattering state, increasing the emitter separation beyond adjacent sites, replacing the single-band dispersion by a multiband dispersion, or increasing the excitation number above two, provided an exact single-excitation solution is available.

source_span.verbatim: The most immediate generalizations are to revisit the multi-photon scattering problem by means of a different initial state; to change the distance between the emitters and investigate delay-induced entangled dark states; or to consider multiband waveguides.

robustness_scope.criterion: For every tuple (g,Δ,J,d) in the claimed subfamily, the analytic amplitudes must satisfy i∂_t|ψ(t)⟩=H|ψ(t)⟩/ℏ in the two-excitation sector with |ψ(0)⟩=a_1†a_2†|0⟩, and the spectrum and decay classification must be obtained from poles and branch points of Ã(ω). A tuple in the hinted superfamily is not counted as solved unless its transformed two-excitation equations reduce to the same C_σ(ω,z) construction or provide an exact single-excitation amplitude that can replace ã_σ(ω) in the parity-resolved secular equation.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_crit∈O_crit, where O_crit is the set of sufficient diagnostic predicates on exact two-excitation trajectories generated by H/ℏ=Δ∑_{j=1}^{2}a_j†a_j−J∑_{j∈ℤ}(b_j†b_{j+1}+b_jb_{j+1}†)+g∑_{j=1}^{2}(a_jb_j†+a_j†b_j)
canonical_goal.target_object: A sufficient threshold witness for collective non-Markovian decay: an exact trajectory |ψ(t)⟩ is certified as displaying behavior beyond independent-excitation decay and beyond the Markovian two-emitter cascade if P_one(t)=∑_{j∈ℤ}(|C_{1,j}(t)|^2+|C_{2,j}(t)|^2)>0.5 for at least one time t≥0
feasibility_constraints: The diagnostic applies to exact trajectories |ψ(t)⟩ generated by H/ℏ=Δ∑_{j=1}^{2}a_j†a_j−J∑_{j∈ℤ}(b_j†b_{j+1}+b_jb_{j+1}†)+g∑_{j=1}^{2}(a_jb_j†+a_j†b_j), with |ψ(0)⟩=a_1†a_2†|0⟩ and the two-excitation expansion |ψ(t)⟩=A(t)a_1†a_2†|0⟩+∑_{j<j'}B_{j,j'}(t)b_j†b_{j'}†|0⟩+∑_{j∈ℤ}B_{j,j}(t)(1/√2)b_j†b_j†|0⟩+∑_{m∈{1,2}}∑_{j∈ℤ}C_{m,j}(t)a_m†b_j†|0⟩.
The diagnostic probability is P_one(t)=∑_{j∈ℤ}(|C_{1,j}(t)|^2+|C_{2,j}(t)|^2), where C_{1,j}(t) and C_{2,j}(t) are the amplitudes for exactly one emitter excitation and one waveguide excitation.

The independent-excitation null model is defined by a scalar p(t)∈[0,1] equal to the probability that one chosen excitation is held by either emitter; under independence, the probability of exactly one emitter-held excitation among two excitations is P_ind(t)=2p(t)(1−p(t)), and max_{p∈[0,1]}2p(1−p)=0.5 because 2p(1−p)=0.5−2(p−0.5)^2.

The Markovian two-emitter null model is defined by a four-state emitter density matrix ρ(t) with memoryless decay-channel rates Γ_1=(1+Δ)Γ, Γ_2=(1−Δ)Γ, Γ_3=(1+Δ)Γ, Γ_4=(1−Δ)Γ, where Γ=2g^2/√(1−Δ^2) for |Δ|<1; its exactly-one-emitter-excited probability is P_M(t)=((1−Δ)/(1+Δ))e^{−(1−Δ)Γt}+((1+Δ)/(1−Δ))e^{−(1+Δ)Γt}−2((1+Δ^2)/(1−Δ^2))e^{−2Γt}, whose global maximum is 0.5 at Δ=0 and Γt=log2.

success_set.definition: Σ_crit={o_crit∈O_crit : o_crit certifies collective non-Markovian decay whenever M(o_crit)>0.5, where M(o_crit)=sup_{t≥0}∑_{j∈ℤ}(|C_{1,j}(t)|^2+|C_{2,j}(t)|^2); the threshold 0.5 is fixed by max_{p∈[0,1]}2p(1−p)=0.5 for independent excitations and by the Markovian two-emitter cascade whose exactly-one-emitter-excited probability has global maximum 0.5 at Δ=0 and Γt=log2. The condition M(o_crit)>0.5 is a sufficient witness, not a necessary definition of all possible collective non-Markovian behavior.}

threshold.metric_definition: M(o_crit)=sup_{t≥0}P_one(t), where P_one(t)=∑_{j∈ℤ}(|C_{1,j}(t)|^2+|C_{2,j}(t)|^2) is computed from the exact two-excitation state |ψ(t)⟩. The numerical value 0.5 is operationally fixed by maximizing 2p(1−p) over p∈[0,1], giving 0.5 at p=0.5, and by the Markovian two-emitter null model whose exactly-one-emitter-excited probability has global maximum 0.5 at Δ=0 and Γt=log2.

source_span.verbatim: Since 2p(1 − p) ≤ 1/2 regardless of the value of p, 0.5 is a fundamental limitation for this probability, were the excitations independent.

source_span.verbatim: In contrast, finding more than a 50% chance of having exactly one emitter excited should be feasible in state-of-the-art experiments while also being a conceptually clearer indicator of collective non-Markovian decay.

robustness_scope.criterion: For a trajectory |ψ(t)⟩ in the claimed diagnostic subfamily, compute P_one(t)=∑_{j∈ℤ}(|C_{1,j}(t)|^2+|C_{2,j}(t)|^2) and M=sup_{t≥0}P_one(t). If M>0.5, then the trajectory violates both the independent-excitation upper bound max_{p∈[0,1]}2p(1−p)=0.5 and the Markovian two-emitter global maximum 0.5, so M>0.5 is a sufficient witness of collective non-Markovian behavior.

methodological_claim.target_object: The derivation is claimed to obtain the exact two-excitation solution by combining transformations of the double complex plane (ω,z), namely inversion (ω,z)↦(ω,z^{−1}), reciprocation (ω,z)↦(−ω,−z), and substitution (ω,z)↦(ω,ζ(ω,z)) with ζ^{±1}(ω,z)=−δω±√(δω+1)√(δω−1) and δω=ω+(z+z^{−1})/2, with the analytic decomposition C_σ(ω,z)=0.5δ^2C_σ(ω,z)(Φ(ω,z)+0.5)−0.5δC_σ(ω,z)+0.5r_σ(ω,z), where δC_σ and δ^2C_σ encode branch jumps, Φ encodes the repeated branch-cut monodromy, and r_σ is the rational remainder after the branch jumps and monodromy are separated.

source_span.verbatim: In this work, we have made an original use of symmetries and analytic methods to solve the problem of two excited QEs coupled to a single-band waveguide.

evidence_channels.formalisation: Define δω=ω+(z+z^{−1})/2 and ζ^{±1}(ω,z)=−δω±√(δω+1)√(δω−1). The methodological claim is that the transformations (ω,z)↦(ω,z^{−1}), (ω,z)↦(−ω,−z), and (ω,z)↦(ω,ζ(ω,z)) identify the branch structure of C_σ(ω,z), and that C_σ(ω,z) is then represented as C_σ(ω,z)=0.5δ^2C_σ(ω,z)(Φ(ω,z)+0.5)−0.5δC_σ(ω,z)+0.5r_σ(ω,z), separating branch jumps, repeated monodromy, and rational remainder.

source_span.paragraph_or_line: Abstract goal sentences; Introduction final paragraph
source_span.verbatim: Here we analyze such a collective non-Markovian decay in a minimal system of two excited emitters coupled to a one-dimensional single-band waveguide. We develop an exact solution for this system in terms of elementary functions that unveils hidden symmetries and predicts new forms of spontaneous decay. The collective non-Markovian dynamics, which are strongly dependent on the vacuum coupling and the detuning from the center of the band, show exotic features that can be characterized with a simple and readily available criterion.

stated_goal.formalisation: The stated formal goal is to construct an exact analytic solution for the two-excitation trajectory |ψ(t)⟩ generated by H/ℏ=Δ∑_{j=1}^{2}a_j†a_j−J∑_{j∈ℤ}(b_j†b_{j+1}+b_jb_{j+1}†)+g∑_{j=1}^{2}(a_jb_j†+a_j†b_j), with |ψ(0)⟩=a_1†a_2†|0⟩, and to use the solution to identify spontaneous-decay phenomena and a sufficient criterion based on sup_{t≥0}∑_{j∈ℤ}(|C_{1,j}(t)|^2+|C_{2,j}(t)|^2)>0.5.

source_span.verbatim: Combining the expression for A˜ in Eqn. (9) with expressions for C˜1,2 (and nested definitions of zσi and ασ) in Tab. I yields A˜(ω) ... for the amplitude of both emitters being simultaneously excited, which we use to study the spectrum and decay properties of the system.

operational_goal.formalisation: The operational formal goal is to solve the transformed two-excitation Schrödinger equations for Ã(ω), B̃_{p,q}(ω), B̃_{q,q}(ω), and C̃_{m,q}(ω); encode C̃_{1,j}(ω) by C(ω,z)=∑_{j∈ℤ}C̃_{1,j}(ω)z^{1−j}; solve the parity-resolved equation C_σ(ω,z)=g(z^{−1}+σ)ã_σ(δω)[0.5+gC̃_{1,2}(ω)/(ω−2Δ)+g∮_{|z'|=1}((z'+σ)/(1+2δωz'+z'^2))C_σ(ω,z')dz'/(2πi)]; obtain Ã(ω); classify bound states, collective exponential poles, continuum branch cuts, algebraic decay, mixed algebraic-exponential decay, and logarithmic corrections from the analytic structure of Ã(ω); and show that P_one(t)=∑_{j∈ℤ}(|C_{1,j}(t)|^2+|C_{2,j}(t)|^2)>0.5 is a sufficient witness beyond independent-excitation and Markovian-null behavior.

inference_basis: The abstract and introduction frame the target as solving the previously unsolved collective non-Markovian decay problem for two initially excited adjacent emitters in a one-dimensional single-band waveguide.

The derivation is organized around the Hamiltonian, two-excitation basis, Wick-rotated transformed amplitudes, C(ω,z), C_σ(ω,z), symmetry transformations, analytic decomposition, and singularity structure of Ã(ω).

The evaluation artefacts are analytic and diagnostic rather than optimization-based: spectra, decay sources, bound-state amplitudes, dynamical plots, and comparison to independent-excitation and Markovian 0.5 bounds.
The conclusion emphasizes the exact transformed-amplitude solution, the variety of decay types, logarithmic corrections, and the experimentally accessible more-than-50% exactly-one-emitter witness.
implicit_goal.formalisation: The implicit best-fit goal is the instrumental pair consisting of (i) exact analytic solution of the two-excitation dynamics for H/ℏ=Δ∑_{j=1}^{2}a_j†a_j−J∑_{j∈ℤ}(b_j†b_{j+1}+b_jb_{j+1}†)+g∑_{j=1}^{2}(a_jb_j†+a_j†b_j), with |ψ(0)⟩=a_1†a_2†|0⟩, and (ii) a sufficient diagnostic witness that collective non-Markovian decay is certified when sup_{t≥0}∑_{j∈ℤ}(|C_{1,j}(t)|^2+|C_{2,j}(t)|^2)>0.5. This pair accounts for the stated aim, formal derivation, spectral analysis, decay classification, bound-state analysis, Markovian comparison, and concluding experimental criterion.

paper_goal.consistency_relation_derivation: The stated channel asks for an exact analytic solution of collective non-Markovian decay in a minimal two-adjacent-emitter single-band waveguide system and for a simple criterion characterizing the resulting dynamics. The operational channel implements those targets through the Hamiltonian, two-excitation expansion, transformed Schrödinger equations, C(ω,z), C_σ(ω,z), analytic-structure decomposition, Ã(ω)-based spectrum and decay analysis, bound-state construction, and the P_one(t)>0.5 sufficient witness. Motivational, application, and speculative generalization statements are excluded rather than treated as formal paper goals.
